content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any listed latency/hardware or rate-allocation documents. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, their Level-1 FPGA latencies in microseconds, and any stated trigger-rate allocation assumptions."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard latency requirement: discard any candidate with latency > 4.0 us. Record each candidate latency as a numeric value, and record a numeric pass/fail flag for latency compliance if useful for later comparison."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every latency-compliant candidate, run simulate_efficiency at coarse thresholds spanning the allowed 20–60 GeV range, for example 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 GeV. Record each returned signal efficiency percentage together with the numeric threshold and candidate identifier code."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best coarse threshold region for each latency-compliant candidate, then run simulate_efficiency on a finer threshold scan around the best region, staying within 20–60 GeV. Use 1–5 GeV spacing depending on the observed variation. Record all efficiencies and thresholds numerically."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated, latency-compliant algorithm/threshold points and select the combination with the highest signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate. If there is a tie within simulation precision, prefer the lower-latency option, then the lower threshold. Record the selected candidate identifier, threshold, efficiency, and latency as numeric values for the reporting module."}]}
